hints.title: Digit Square Sum Cycle Detection
hints.text: Repeatedly replacing a number with the sum of squares of its digits either terminates at 1 or loops indefinitely in a cycle. What traversal technique detects repeating states?

hints.title: Tortoise and Hare Cycle Invariant
hints.text: Moving a slow pointer one step and a fast pointer two steps will inevitably cause both to meet inside any repeating cycle.

hints.title: Stepwise Cycle Detection Procedure
hints.text: Define helper to calculate sum of squared digits of a number. Initialize slow to n and fast to helper(n). While fast is not 1 and slow does not equal fast, advance slow by one step and fast by two steps. Return true if fast reached 1, otherwise false.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def isHappy(self, n: int) -> bool:
        def get_next(val):
            total = 0
            while val > 0:
                d = val % 10
                total += d * d
                val //= 10
            return total
        slow = n
        fast = get_next(n)
        while fast != 1 and slow != fast:
            slow = get_next(slow)
            fast = get_next(get_next(fast))
        return fast == 1
```

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(log N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Maintaining a history collection uses unbounded memory when numbers cycle.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Floyd cycle detection finds the loop in O(log N) iterations with O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that the sequence must cycle and apply Floyd cycle detection.
